title: Telangana SIR: Who Is Missing From the Draft Rolls?
shows: Frontline reports a preliminary analysis that the Sabar Institute shared with it, of the names left off Telangana's draft roll in the 104 Assembly seats outside Hyderabad. Sabar compiled the Election Commission's booth-wise lists of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors and counted 53,96,806 names against the Commission's 53,97,791, and its total matched the Commission's in 31 of 32 districts. By its count about 50.2 per cent of the names are women's, and more women than men were left off in 91 of the 104 seats. It describes about 71 per cent of those women as married, with an average age of about 45, and the article does not say how Sabar worked out marital status, which the roll does not record. It counts 1,152 third gender electors among the names left off, and Frontline gives 2,350 on Telangana's 2023 roll. It puts 85.8 per cent of the names, 46.31 lakh, as marked shifted, untraceable or already enrolled elsewhere. Sabar also classifies the names by religion, and it counts a name as Muslim only where both the Telugu and the English spelling on the roll point to it. By that classification Muslim names are 12.5 per cent of the names left off, in districts where the 2011 Census puts Muslims at 8.8 per cent. In the seven seats the BJP won in 2023 they are nearly 45 per cent of the names marked untraceable and 17 per cent of those marked dead. Sabar finds 202 booths where more than 90 per cent of the names left off are Muslim names, and 512 of 532 booths it examined where more than 95 per cent carry one reason, permanently shifted. Its lead researcher, Sabir Ahamed, tells Frontline that the figures show an association with these characteristics and cannot show a cause.
quote: Analysis of State-wide data (excluding Hyderabad) also showed that around 50.2 per cent of the names on the deletions list are of women.
In 91 out of the 104 seats outside Hyderabad, Sabar found that more women than men featured on the deletions list.
About 71 per cent of the “deleted” women voters were married and, on average, aged around 45 years.
In total, Sabar analysed 53,96,806 deleted names against the ECI’s 53,97,791, missing the analysis for only 985 out of nearly 54 lakh deletions from across the state (barring Hyderabad).
A voter was counted as bearing a Muslim name only when both the Telugu spelling and the English (Romanised) spelling (in the electoral rolls) bore out the conclusion.
note: First reading, 4 November 2026. The page was read in full with curl (the article body from the HTML, and the AMP page, which carries the same text). Published 19 September 2026 at 8:14 pm IST (article:published_time 2026-09-19T20:14:45+05:30), byline Ayesha Minhaz, isAccessibleForFree true. The figures are Sabar's, from an exclusive preliminary analysis the institute shared with Frontline, and the summary attributes each to Sabar. No report on Telangana outside Hyderabad is on sabarinstitute.org: the institute's publication list (admin.sabarinstitute.org/api/research-and-publications, 14 records on 4 November 2026) holds the Hyderabad report of 1 September, already in sabar.json, and nothing for the other 104 seats, so the article is the only published source. The 3 November press conference of the Telangana Voter Rights Forum was not found to carry these figures in the reports read (Countercurrents and Deccan Herald of 3 November). Checked against the site's data. The Commission's 53,97,791 is the rest_of_state count in data/hyderabad/telangana.json, so Sabar's 53,96,806 is 985 short, 0.02 per cent. The article's state figures agree with data/india/states.json: 3,38,26,448 electors before the revision, 21.7 per cent left off (21.6967), 16.99 per cent absent or shifted (57,46,803), 2.73 per cent dead (9,22,229) and 1.98 per cent duplicate (6,70,203). Its 92,87,577 notices differ by 610 from the 92,88,187 notices generated in telangana.json's hearings_press, which is the Chief Electoral Officer's later figure as Telangana Today reported it. 46.31 lakh is 85.8 per cent of 53,97,791. Sabar's 31 of 32 districts matches the 32 districts outside Hyderabad in telangana.json. The article does not say whether the 2,350 third gender electors are the whole state or the 104 seats, so the summary gives the number as Frontline does. Religion is Sabar's classification by names, by string matching and a cross-check of the Telugu and English spellings, with a name marked uncertain where only one agrees. Marital status is also Sabar's classification, and the article does not say how it was made. The article's word is deleted, and the summary uses left off. The article also reports the Chief Electoral Officer's comment, the claims deadline of 7 October and the final roll then due on 9 November, which have since moved.
